title: The gear you carry
summary: R.E.P.O. is a game about carrying things, including your own equipment: the game defines a walkie-talkie, a revive item, a ladder and a rideable vehicle as separate pieces of gear.
body: Gear is made of individual items rather than one inventory screen, so what you bring is a physical decision about the run.
A revive item is its own object, which is why bringing someone back is tied to having the item rather than being a free action.
Some gear moves you rather than your hands: a ladder and a rideable vehicle are their own objects too.

Every piece of gear is described the same way. An item carries a name and a localised name, a type, an emoji icon, a maximum amount and a maximum in the shop, a minimum crew size and purchase limits, a spawn rotation offset and a flag for whether it is a physical object, which is why the same machinery serves a walkie-talkie and a ladder.

Gear is shown and announced as well as carried. An equippable item has its own icon, obstruction layers and emoji, and carries a flag for whether it pings an inventory and one for whether that ping is played for everybody, which is why a crew can be told about a find.
What this entry does not tell you: prices, how many items you can carry or how much a revive restores. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A walkie-talkie is a defined item you can carry.
Reviving a crew member uses a dedicated item.
A ladder is its own piece of gear.
There is a rideable vehicle item.

Every item carries a name and a localised name, a type, an emoji icon, a maximum amount and a maximum in the shop, a minimum crew size, purchase limits, a spawn rotation offset and a flag for being a physical object.
